summary.scope: Read-only review of every public marketing/content route except /sign-in, all source-defined variants, FAQs and changelog entries, shared navigation/metadata, simulator branches, invalid paths, machine-readable endpoints, and historical-domain redirects.
summary.method: Source-only review; targeted worker/API traces and selected current primary-source checks. Parent separately verifies rendered desktop/mobile/light/dark pages. No source files changed by this reviewer.
summary.assessment: The homepage now has clearer distinct purposes for each section and retains its original hero/voice. Launch concerns are specific action guarantees, one demo count, recovery consistency, and a few destination/label issues; a wholesale rewrite is unnecessary.
purposefulRepetition: Header, hero, and final Start free actions serve different page positions and can stay.
Topic-specific simulator CTAs connect guides/comparisons to the relevant sample rather than merely duplicate a generic CTA.
Site navigation and one in-page guide CTA are useful different entry points; do not remove both solely because they share a destination.

claimChecks.plans: Public plan amounts/capabilities and purchase availability compared to shared tier/pricing manifests and runtime CTA branches, not live catalog or checkout.
claimChecks.privacy: Published no-full-content, subject/snippet, Anthropic, analytics-consent and unsubscribe distinctions compared to shared canonical copy and referenced implementation/context.
claimChecks.external: Selected vendor and Google claims were checked against primary sources today; this was not a complete independent verification of every competitor feature, price, or linked source. No external claim was promoted to a finding without contradictory evidence.

summary.productionMarkersAndBaseUrls: No unintended localhost/staging/TODO/placeholder marketing copy found in reviewed source. Fictional sample domains are explicitly labelled. siteUrl defaults to https://declutrmail.com but honors NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL; OAuth API origin is environment-controlled. Exact deployed origins, availability, billing rails, Google approval receipt, email delivery and live provider behavior remain unverified by this reviewer.
limitations: Browser screenshots, DOM, accessibility, mobile layout, interaction and production host tests are owned by the parent; none are claimed here.
Authentication, onboarding and core authenticated app surfaces are assigned to other reviewers; /sign-in is explicitly excluded.
Existing untracked records-prototype code is not part of the marketing route inventory reviewed here.
No paid checkout, live write, unsubscribe request, Gmail mutation, or external message was sent.
Security/privacy/legal copy was checked for repository consistency, not supplied as legal advice or certification.

findings.state: Manual sender action between preview and execution
findings.title: Published Gmail recheck guarantee is stronger than the worker implementation

evidence.detail: Canonical action-preview copy says DeclutrMail checks Gmail again when the action runs.
Terms specifically says the worker re-checks Gmail at execution.
Machine-readable pricing repeats the execution-time Gmail check.
Static public summary repeats the same guarantee.
Sender selector is resolved again by resolveSenderActionIds.
resolveSenderActionIds selects provider IDs from the local mailMessages database using senderActionWhere; it does not fetch current Gmail scope.
The resolved local IDs are passed directly to Gmail batchModify.
batchModify only posts the supplied IDs and label changes in chunks; it performs no Gmail message-scope read.

findings.recommendation: Remove the claim that Gmail is rechecked. Describe that the matching scope is resolved again when execution starts and the final count can differ, or implement and verify an actual provider recheck before retaining the guarantee. Keep the current-index wording in the Delete guide; that wording matches the implementation.
findings.verification: Source trace from selector resolution through Gmail mutation adapter; no provider mutation or production freshness test performed. A Gmail label-name lookup is not a current message-scope recheck.
findings.launchImpact: A user may approve a preview believing the provider is freshly checked. This trust guarantee should match the implementation before launch.

findings.route: All public routes via SoftwareApplication JSON-LD; /pricing.md
findings.state: Structured data and machine-readable action semantics
findings.title: Public machine-readable copy promises a preview for every action

evidence.detail: Both description branches claim every action is previewed, then include Keep among the five decisions; both also mention Activity recovery only for Archive and Later.
Every Unsubscribe action is described as showing a matching count/sample/exact Gmail change, even when no backlog cleanup is selected.
Visible guide correctly says Keep is inline and affected-email previews apply to mail-moving actions.
Keep is explicitly never previewed.
The live affected-email preview gate covers Archive, Later, Delete, and Unsubscribe only when historic Archive is selected.
Canonical recovery claim includes Activity Undo for Delete.

findings.recommendation: Align JSON-LD and pricing markdown with the visible guide: Keep records an inline decision; mail-moving actions show the affected-email preview; unsubscribe confirms its method and any optional separate cleanup. Include Delete with Archive/Later when listing Activity Undo.
findings.verification: Compared shared JSON-LD and markdown against production ActionSheet branches, visible product guide, and canonical recovery copy. Source-only.
findings.launchImpact: Search/answer-engine summaries can repeat product behavior that disagrees with the visible page and application.

findings.state: Completed demo after Delete with Inbox + archived
findings.title: Demo outcome counts archived mail as cleared from Inbox

evidence.detail: affectedCount includes syntheticArchivedCount when Delete reach is all_mail.
OutcomeSummary sums the entire affectedCount into clearedFromInbox.
That total is labelled Cleared from Inbox.

findings.recommendation: Track inbox-removed count separately from total affected count, or label the total as Emails acted on. Verify the completed summary for Delete with archived reach and for Archive/Later/unsubscribe-with-backlog.
findings.verification: Deterministic source calculation: archived messages contribute to the value despite already being outside Inbox. Parent can reproduce with the guided Delete sample and complete the tour.
findings.launchImpact: The demo teaches an incorrect outcome metric for a supported action scope.

findings.title: Guided-tour query does not select the workspace that renders the tour

evidence.detail: Workspace defaults to Senders.
Only workspace=triage or a step query selects Triage.
tour=1 selects guided mode without selecting Triage.
SendersSimulator renders while workspace is Senders; the guided tour is in the other branch.
Changing demo mode uses tour=1 as its URL representation.

findings.recommendation: When parsing tour=1, select Triage as well as guided mode. Preserve an explicit Senders choice only if that query combination is intentionally supported and documented.
findings.verification: Source state initialization and render-branch trace; step=1–4 already sets the required workspace. No runtime assertion by this reviewer.
findings.launchImpact: A shared direct tour URL can open the sender workspace instead of the promised guided experience.

findings.state: Paired unsubscribe with separate Archive or Delete
findings.title: Recovery explanation omits Activity Undo for a paired Delete

evidence.detail: The guide explicitly supports a secondary Archive or Delete in the unsubscribe confirmation.
Recovery paragraph says only the archive portion is reversible while its Activity window is open and then gives Delete only Gmail Trash recovery.
Lifecycle note only says a paired Archive has its own Undo, despite Delete being a supported paired cleanup.
Delete can be undone from Activity until its displayed deadline; Trash is an additional fallback.

findings.recommendation: Say that a separate Archive or Delete has its own Activity Undo until its deadline, while the sent unsubscribe request cannot be recalled. Preserve the distinction with Trash without adding a longer caveat.
findings.verification: Compared guide, lifecycle figure, and canonical recovery semantics. Source-only; no actual unsubscribe request sent.
findings.launchImpact: A user deciding whether to include Delete can infer a more limited recovery path than the product offers.

findings.title: Daily-review CTA lands in the default Senders demo

evidence.detail: Try the daily review demo links to bare /inbox-simulator.
Bare simulator URL starts in Senders; Daily Triage is a separate workspace.

findings.recommendation: Link this CTA to /inbox-simulator?workspace=triage, or change its label to match the sender workspace.
findings.verification: Source destination versus simulator default state; no navigation performed by this reviewer.
findings.launchImpact: Visitors following the named daily-review path must discover and switch to a different workspace.

findings.title: Autopilot guide asks readers to enable the same rule twice

evidence.detail: First step is Turn on review.
Second step waits for representative traffic after the preset is enabled.
Third step says to review the sample before turning on the rule.

findings.recommendation: Place the activation preview in the first step. Make the third step review the collected suggestions, names, and exceptions rather than repeat the pre-activation instruction.
findings.verification: Read the complete ordered steps and preceding always-Observe explanation. Source-only.
findings.launchImpact: The learning path is harder to follow even though the underlying always-review behavior is correctly explained.

findings.state: Privacy & control section, then expanded inventory
findings.title: Homepage privacy summary repeats the same data boundary

evidence.detail: The lede states the canonical no-full-email-contents boundary.
A nearby Full messages stay in Gmail item repeats the same no-full-email-contents claim.
Expanded data inventory renders another full PrivacyBadge card.
Repository copy budget puts trust/privacy copy once per flow at its decision point.

findings.recommendation: Keep one clear boundary in the section lede and use the summary for distinct facts such as the stored fields, access controls, and decision controls. Let the disclosure add the full inventory rather than duplicate its introduction. Keep useful Start free repetition in header/hero/final CTA.
findings.verification: Adjacent visible source copy plus expanded disclosure; this is a focused duplication finding, not a recommendation for a homepage rewrite.
findings.launchImpact: Minor reading burden on the mobile section and one less distinct reason to scan each summary item.

findings.state: Shared topic demo buttons and simulator controls
findings.title: Several button labels exceed the repository copy budget

evidence.detail: Try an unsubscribe preview has four words; the other topic labels at lines 7, 10, and 12 also have four.
Where this fits in your workspace uses six words.
Preview the Autopilot rule uses four words.
Explore all sample senders uses four words.
Button or menu item budget is three words or fewer.

findings.recommendation: Use short, destination-specific labels such as Preview Unsubscribe, Preview automation, Delete and recovery, Try Senders, Workspace guide, Preview rule, and Explore senders. Keep article titles and explanatory prose descriptive.
findings.verification: Word count of actual button/CTA strings against explicit repository budget; no assumption that every prose link is a button.
findings.launchImpact: Small but repeated scanability issue across many generated pages and mobile demo controls.

findings.title: Waitlist error claims a network failure for every failed request

evidence.detail: All thrown errors use the same generic error state.
The displayed error says the server could not be reached.
The form delegates to apiPost, whose rejected responses include server HTTP errors as well as network failures.
ApiError represents any non-2xx response; a responding server can therefore produce this state.

findings.recommendation: Use a truthful generic failure with a next action, such as Couldn’t join the waitlist. Try again., or distinguish verified network and server causes.
findings.verification: Source catch/error-class trace; rejection states were not injected by this reviewer.
findings.launchImpact: A visitor can receive an inaccurate failure diagnosis and no useful distinction for retrying.
